title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood in Austin, Texas. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle during the incident. The vehicle did not slow down or stop before hitting the duck, which was nesting near a local restaurant and had become known to residents.

The failure occurred in the perception and response systems of the deployed vehicle. Whether the autonomous system failed to detect the duck, detected it but did not classify it as an obstacle requiring evasion, or could not execute an emergency stop in time is not established by the reporting. A system tested only in simulation before deployment to public streets, or one without requirements for detecting small animals in its operational domain, would have allowed this outcome.

It is not established whether the vehicle's behavior reflected a gap in training data, a deficiency in the model's ability to generalize to novel situations, insufficient sensor range or resolution, or a decision by the system's designers about what obstacles warrant emergency response.

Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant concern from residents about self-driving car safety. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck, which was nesting outside a local Italian restaurant, had become familiar to neighborhood residents, intensifying their reaction to its death. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and stated it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the car failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets near the lake from its service area. Avride is now conducting controlled experiments in simulation to improve its technology and prevent similar situations while ensuring safety remains unaffected. Other companies including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate autonomous vehicles in Austin.
